decisions.reason: The panel power-button clause is an independent decision already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE; changing DCDC1 to 3.4V does not alter the button connector or control behavior.
The DCDC1 adjustment compensates for the main-board Schottky drop and explicitly preserves the shared rail at 3.3V; the standalone LDO behavior and source-selection topology remain unchanged.
The current monitor remains after the Schottky diodes and continues measuring the downstream 3.3V rail; the source changes upstream DCDC1 regulation, not monitoring coverage, placement, or channels.

The source does not change any connector, pin order, pinout, or board-distribution topology. The existing 3V3 pin designation need not change merely because its upstream DCDC1 source is configured to compensate for a downstream diode drop.
The DCDC1 voltage compensation does not alter the ESP32 BOOT button, reset connection, or associated capacitance requirements.
The source changes the configured DCDC1 output voltage but does not change the candidate's USB-to-VMID path, VMID/VSYS topology, battery voltage, or normal-operation power-path relationship.
The DCDC1 regulation change does not alter the selected ESP32-S3 module or its breakout requirement.
The source concerns power-rail compensation and does not change USB enumeration, programming, or the USB-C programming interface.
The source changes AXP2101 DCDC1 for the 3.3V path and does not alter the independently switched 5V boost rail, its GPIO control, loads, or shutdown behavior.
The compensated system rail remains 3.3V downstream, so the sensor-board connector inventory and its 3V3 power pins remain valid unchanged.
The source preserves the downstream 3.3V rail and does not change I2C pull-up voltage, resistance, location, bus speed, cable length, or series-resistor policy.
The LED requirement uses the separate 5V supply and its data-level-shifter decision is unaffected by the DCDC1 compensation for the 3.3V rail.
